Holly uses stacks to manage shoeboxes containing shoes of different sizes. For example, the following stack has 4 shoeboxes, with a pair of shoes of size 35, 37, 38 and 40 in each box respectively.
40
38
37
35
← Bottom of the stack
Below are the sub-programs Holly uses to manipulate the stacks:
Sub-program
Description
push(S, z)
Push a box containing shoes of size z into stack S.
pop(S)
Remove a box from stack S and return the size of the shoes in the box.
isEmpty(S)
Return True if stack S is empty, otherwise False.
isFull(S)
Return True if stack S is full, otherwise False.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Holly wants to stack the shoeboxes in ascending order of size of the shoes stored. The following is the content of stack M:
42
41
37
39
36
36
Stack M
At the bottom of the stack is the 1st box. Which two boxes need to be swapped in stack M?(1 mark)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Holly develops a sub-program swap(S, x) to help swap the xth and the (x+1)th box in stack S.

parts.label: i
parts.text:
She uses an empty stack T to help with the operation of swap(S, x). Help Holly finish the pseudocode for swap(S, x).(4 marks)
Line  Pseudocode

8            push(S, pop(T))

parts.label: ii
parts.text:

[--Answer:
(a) 3rd, 4th
(b)(i)
x

temp
x-1

Ellen develops a web application for a popular concert’s online ticketing system. When the number of users simultaneously using the application reaches a certain threshold, new users are directed to the queuing page before they are granted access to the application. Ellen uses an array P with indexes from 0 to n-1 to store the queue of users, and uses the following variables and sub-programs to process array P:

This global variable stores the number of waiting guests.

This global variable stores the index in P for the next new user.

Sub-program to add a new user’s id uid to P if P is not full. The item after P[N-1] is P[0].

items.stem:
A palindrome (回文) is a word, phrase or sentence that looks the same both backwards and forwards. For example, the word “madam” is a palindrome. Henry is developing a program in Python that can be used to check if the input string is a palindrome. He creates a stack r and uses stack manipulation in the program.
Stack r
Refer to the following sub-programs for stack manipulation:
Sub-program
Description
push(r, c)
Push an item c into stack r.
pop(r)
Take an item from stack r and return that item.
isEmpty(r)
Return True if there are no items in stack r; otherwise, return False.

parts.label: i
parts.text:
To reverse the order of the letters in a word, Henry uses the stack r by pushing the letters into it and popping the letters out.
After executing the following algorithm, write down the content of stack r.(1 mark)
push(r, "w")
push(r, "o")
push(r, "w")
Stack r

parts.label: ii
parts.text:
To simplify the above algorithm, Henry creates a sub-program pushString(r, s) to push the whole string s (whose index starts from 1) into stack r. Complete the pseudocode for the sub-program pushString(r, s).(2 marks)
Sub-program pushString(r, s)
for i from 1 to length of s
push(r, _____)

parts.label: iii
parts.text:
Henry then creates another sub-program popString(r) to pop all the letters in stack r and put them together as a word. Complete the pseudocode for the sub-program popString(r).(1 mark)
Sub-program popString(r)
s  ""
while not(___________)
s  _______________
return s

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Henry implements a sub-program check(s) to return True if a string s is a palindrome or return False if not. Complete the pseudocode for the sub-program check(s).(1 mark)
Sub-program check(s)
pushString(r, s)
ns  popString(r)
if _______________ then
return True
else
return False
[--Answer:
(a)(i)
"w"
"o"
"w"
Stack r
(a)(ii) s[i]
(a)(iii)
isEmpty(r)
s + pop(r)
(b) ns = s
--]

During the add-drop period of a university, the course enrolment system uses an array waitlist to store the student IDs of students who wish to enrol on a course if that course is full at the moment. The data in the array is processed with circular queue data structure, that means the item after the last array item is waitlist[0].
The following variables and sub-programs are used in the course enrolment system to process array waitlist:
Variable / Sub-program
Description
N
This global variable stores the number of students on the waitlist.
first
This global variable stores the array index of the first student on the waitlist.
last
This global variable stores the array index of the last student on the waitlist.
enq(l, sid)
If queue l is not full, this sub-program saves a new student ID sid at the last position in the queue.
deq(l)
If queue l is not empty, this sub-program returns the student ID of the first student on the queue.
There are 10 places on array waitlist. Assume that first = 8 and last = 7, the waitlist for the course COMP1001 is shown below:
